q: Railway freight rates in India are primarily based on which charging factor?
Classification of goods for freight purposes divides commodities into:
A commodity placed in a higher class attracts:

options.A: A lower freight rate per tonne-km
options.B: The same rate as all other classes
options.C: A higher freight rate than a lower class

q: The 'minimum weight for charge' rule ensures that:

options.A: Freight is charged on at least the prescribed minimum weight of the wagon used
options.B: Every consignment weighs at least one tonne
options.D: Freight is waived below the minimum

q: Tapered (telescopic) rates in railway freight mean that:

options.B: The per-km rate falls as distance increases
options.D: Rates are fixed regardless of distance

q: Chargeable distance for freight is reckoned on the basis of:

options.A: The actual route the train takes
options.B: Road distance between the two cities
options.C: A fixed distance for every state
options.D: The shortest rail route between booking and destination stations

q: When goods are carried via a longer route at the consignor's request, freight is charged on:
The Goods Tariff is the document that contains:

options.C: Freight rates, classification and charging rules

q: Freight on a consignment is generally computed on:

options.B: Chargeable weight multiplied by the applicable rate

q: Surcharges and development charges on freight are:

options.D: Levied in addition to the base freight rate

q: A 'class rate' in railway freight terminology refers to the rate:

options.A: Applicable to a particular classification class of goods

q: Commodities not specifically classified in the tariff are charged at:

options.C: A general prescribed class rate for unclassified goods

q: A wagonload rate applies when:

options.B: Goods fill a wagon to the prescribed minimum weight

q: Trainload rates are generally:

options.A: Lower than wagonload rates per tonne
options.B: Higher than wagonload rates per tonne

q: To earn a trainload rate, the consignor must normally offer:

options.D: A full train or the prescribed minimum number of wagons

q: The main commercial advantage of trainload rates to the railway is:

options.C: Better wagon utilization and reduced handling cost

q: If a trainload consignment falls short of the minimum wagon requirement:

options.A: It still gets the trainload rate
options.B: It is charged at the wagonload rate

q: Smalls (less than wagonload) consignments are charged:

options.A: At smalls scale rates higher per unit than wagonload

q: The Railway Receipt (RR) is:

options.D: The document acknowledging receipt of goods for carriage by rail

q: An RR is issued at the:

options.B: Booking station when goods are accepted

q: Essential contents of an RR include:

options.C: Consignor, consignee, description, weight, stations and freight terms

q: A 'freight paid' RR means:

options.A: Freight has been paid at the booking station
options.B: Freight will be collected at destination
options.D: Freight is paid to the driver

q: A 'freight to-pay' RR means:

options.B: Freight is collected from the consignee at destination
options.D: Freight is paid by the guard

q: Delivery of goods at destination is normally made against:
If the original RR is lost, delivery may be given on:

options.C: An indemnity bond executed by the claimant

q: The RR serves as:

options.A: A document of title to the goods it covers
options.B: Only a receipt, not a document of title

q: Duplicate RRs are issued:

options.B: Only in prescribed circumstances with safeguards against double delivery

q: Endorsement of an RR by the consignee permits:
Terminal charges in freight are levied to cover:

options.C: Handling and terminal services at stations and sidings

q: A private siding is:

options.A: A rail track connecting a private premises to the railway system

q: Siding charges are generally payable by:

options.B: The siding owner or user for facilities and services provided

q: Demurrage is charged when:

options.D: Wagons are detained beyond the prescribed free time for loading or unloading

q: Wharfage is levied on:

options.C: Goods not removed from railway premises within free time

q: Free time for loading and unloading is allowed to:

options.A: Give a reasonable period before demurrage or wharfage applies

q: At the booking station, freight collected on 'paid' consignments is:

options.B: Accounted as station earnings and remitted per procedure

q: The outward goods records at a station primarily serve to:

options.D: Account for every consignment booked and freight collected

q: Inward goods accounts at destination capture:

options.C: To-pay freight collected and deliveries made

q: A station's goods earnings are remitted to the railway through:

options.A: Prescribed remittance procedure to the cash office or bank

q: The 'goods cash book' at a station records:

options.B: All cash transactions relating to goods traffic

q: Weighment of consignments at booking is important because:

options.D: Freight is weight-based, so correct weight ensures the correct charge

q: Re-weighment en route or at destination is done to:

options.C: Detect under-declaration of weight and recover correct freight

q: Station outstanding freight not yet collected must be:

options.A: Shown and pursued as dues recoverable

q: The station balance sheet is:

options.A: A personal account of the station master
options.B: A statement of a station's earnings, remittances and outstandings

q: In the station balance sheet, freight collected appears on the:
Remittances made by the station appear as:

options.C: Deductions from the balance due from the station

q: The closing balance of a station balance sheet represents:

options.A: Cash and outstandings still held due from the station

q: The opening balance of a station balance sheet is:

options.B: The closing balance of the previous period

q: The Traffic Accounts office uses station balance sheets to:

options.D: Verify station earnings, remittances and outstandings

q: An undercharge occurs when:

options.C: Less freight than due is collected on a consignment

q: An overcharge occurs when:

options.A: More freight than due is collected from the customer

q: Undercharges detected are raised as:

options.B: Dues recoverable through undercharge statements and bills

q: Common causes of undercharge include:

options.D: Wrong classification, wrong rate or short weighment

q: Overcharges detected are dealt with by:

options.C: Refunding the excess to the party entitled

q: The Traffic Accounts office detects undercharges and overcharges by:

options.A: Test-checking station documents against tariff rules

q: Refund of freight is admissible when:

options.B: Excess or incorrect freight was collected under prescribed conditions

q: A claim for refund of freight must normally be made:

options.D: Within the prescribed time limit with supporting documents

q: Refund on a 'to-pay' consignment not taken delivery of may arise when:

options.C: Charges were wrongly levied though delivery was not taken

q: Before sanctioning a refund, the accounts office verifies:

options.A: The correctness of the claim against station records and the tariff

q: Refunds sanctioned are accounted as:

options.B: Deductions from earnings in station accounts

q: Double payment of freight collected at both ends is resolved by:

options.D: Refunding the duplicate collection after verification

q: On Indian Railways, freight is generally charged on which of the following bases?

options.A: Distance and chargeable weight as per the Goods Tariff
options.B: Owner's declared value of the consignment
options.C: A flat rate per wagon regardless of distance
options.D: Number of axles multiplied by loading time

q: 'Chargeable weight' of a consignment is normally determined as?

options.A: The actual weight declared by the sender
options.B: The maximum of actual weight, minimum weight condition, and volumetrics where applicable
options.C: The wagon's carrying capacity divided by four

q: Why do goods tariffs prescribe minimum weight conditions?

options.A: To encourage booking in full wagon loads rather than small lots
options.B: To penalise consignors for late delivery
options.C: To ensure a fair return on wagon space even when partly loaded
options.D: To fix the maximum load a wagon can carry

q: A consignor books less than the minimum weight for a wagon. How is freight recovered?

options.A: Freight is charged only on the actual weight loaded
options.B: The booking is refused and no freight is charged
options.C: Freight is charged at half the minimum weight rate
options.D: Freight is charged on the minimum weight condition

q: 'Demurrage' in goods traffic refers to charges levied for?

options.A: Detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for loading or unloading
options.B: Late arrival of the goods train at destination
options.C: Overloading of wagons beyond permissible capacity

q: Who is primarily responsible for loading and unloading of full wagon consignments?

options.B: The consignor/consignee unless the tariff specifies otherwise
options.D: The goods guard of the train

q: 'Terminal charges' in the Goods Tariff cover which services?

options.A: Haulage of the train between stations
options.B: Insurance of the consignment during transit
options.C: Handling, stacking, and supervision at loading/unloading terminals

q: Transhipment of goods at a break-of-gauge station becomes necessary because?

options.A: The consignee requests a different destination
options.B: The goods are perishable and need faster movement
options.C: The freight rate changes at the junction
options.D: Wagons cannot run through between different gauges, so goods are transferred

q: Who bears the cost of transhipment at a break-of-gauge station under normal tariff rules?

options.A: The consignor/consignee through the tariff rate or a separate charge
options.C: The receiving railway division's operating budget
options.D: No one; transhipment is always free

q: Rebooking (diversion) of a goods consignment en route is permitted when?

options.A: Never; destination cannot change once booked
options.B: On the consignee's request with railway approval, on payment of prescribed charges
options.C: Only if the original destination station is closed
options.D: Automatically whenever the consignee sells the goods

q: On rebooking of goods to a farther destination, the additional freight recovered is?

options.A: Nil; the original freight covers any diversion
options.C: Freight for the additional distance at the applicable rate

q: Delivery of goods at destination is made to whom under railway rules?

options.B: The consignor who booked the goods
options.C: The first person arriving at the goods shed
options.D: The consignee named in the railway receipt or the endorsed holder

q: Before delivery of a consignment, the railway is entitled to recover?

options.A: All outstanding dues: freight, demurrage, wharfage, and other charges
options.B: Only the freight shown on the railway receipt
options.C: A delivery fee equal to the freight
options.D: Nothing; charges are collected after delivery

q: 'Wharfage' is charged in goods sheds for?

options.B: Goods not removed from railway premises within the free time allowed
options.C: Loading of wagons at private sidings

q: A claim for loss or damage to goods must generally be preferred within what period?

options.C: Within six months from the date the goods were entrusted to the railway

q: For compensation claims, the railway's liability for goods is limited to?

options.A: The market value at destination in all cases
options.C: The insurance premium paid by the consignor
options.D: The value declared or as assessed under the Railways Act provisions

q: 'Owner's risk' rates in the Goods Tariff mean that?

options.A: The railway's liability is limited as the goods move at the owner's risk
options.B: The railway accepts full liability for loss or damage
options.C: The owner must insure the goods with the railway
options.D: Freight is charged at double the normal rate

q: The railway is NOT liable for loss of goods arising from?

options.B: Act of God, war, or inherent vice of the goods

q: In traffic accounts, freight earnings from goods are credited to which head?
Freight collected 'to pay' (freight payable at destination) is accounted by the destination station through?

options.B: A debit to the consignor's account
options.D: The goods outward returns and collection by the destination station

q: A 'railway receipt' (RR) serves as?

options.A: Evidence of the contract of carriage and title to claim delivery
options.B: A negotiable instrument like a cheque
options.C: An insurance policy for the goods
options.D: A pass for the goods guard

q: If goods are over-carried beyond the booked destination, the railway should?

options.B: Bring the goods back to the destination station without extra charge

q: Short delivery of a consignment is settled in accounts by?

options.C: Recording the shortage and settling the claim for the missing quantity

q: 'Siding charges' relate to?

options.D: Wagons placed in private or assisted sidings for loading/unloading

q: The 'weighment' of a wagon load is done to?

options.A: Verify the chargeable weight for correct freight assessment
options.B: Check the speed of the goods train

q: When a weighbridge shows weight above the declared weight, the station should?

options.B: Recover undercharges on the excess as per rules
options.D: Return the wagon to the consignor

q: Overloading of a wagon beyond its permissible carrying capacity attracts?

options.A: No action if the goods reach safely
options.B: A warning to the consignor only
options.C: Overloading charges and possible transhipment of the excess

q: 'Crane charges' in goods traffic are levied for?

options.D: Use of railway cranes for loading/unloading heavy articles

q: In case of damage to goods in transit noticed at destination, the first step is?

options.A: Record the damage on the delivery book and issue a certificate of damage
options.D: Send the goods back to the booking station

q: Perishable goods arriving at destination and not taken delivery of may be?

options.A: Kept indefinitely in the goods shed
options.B: Sold by auction after notice to protect their value

q: Sale proceeds of auctioned unclaimed goods are adjusted in which order?

options.B: Divided equally between railway and consignee
options.C: Railway dues first, balance to the person entitled
options.D: Credited to the staff welfare fund

q: 'Through booking' of goods means?

options.A: Booking only on a single railway
options.C: Booking of parcels by passenger train
options.D: Booking over more than one railway under a single railway receipt

q: In through goods traffic, freight earnings are shared between railways by?

options.A: Apportionment based on distance carried as per junction agreements
options.C: The booking railway keeps the entire freight
options.D: The destination railway keeps the entire freight

q: The station accounts for goods earnings are compiled from?

options.B: Daily and monthly goods returns: invoices, railway receipts, and collection summaries

q: 'Paid' freight (freight paid at booking) is credited to earnings by?

options.C: The booking station at the time of collection

q: A consignment booked at 'railway risk' rate carries higher freight because?

options.B: The goods are always insured privately
options.D: The railway accepts wider liability for loss or damage

q: 'Lump sum' rates for full train loads are offered mainly to?

options.A: Encourage bulk movement and simplify charging

q: If a consignor cancels a booking before the wagon is supplied?

options.B: Only prescribed cancellation or registration charges apply
options.D: Demurrage for seven days is charged

q: Wagon registration fee (WRF) is collected for?

options.C: Registering an indent for supply of wagons

q: Demurrage is generally NOT charged when detention is caused by?

options.B: Late arrival of the consignee's trucks
options.D: Railway's inability to supply locomotives or clear wagons
